title: Acoustic Cavitation-Induced Unfolding and Solubilization of Velvet Antler Protein for Antioxidant Peptide Release: Substrate Modification Kinetics, Quantum Chemistry, and Keap1/Nrf2-Associated Cellular Responses.
authors: Xin, Xuanying; Wang, Haowen; Park, Sungkwon; Yan, Changguo; Li, Qiang; Du, Rui; Li, Xiangzi
one_liner_zh: 该文研究超声空化处理鹿茸蛋白以释放抗氧化肽，涉及DFT和分子对接但对象为蛋白-小分子肽及Keap1蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: The targeted extraction of bioactive peptides from structurally robust biological matrices, such as velvet antler protein (VAP), is severely hindered by high steric hindrance and profound conformational stability. This study established a multiscale analytical framework to investigate ultrasound-assisted VAP modification and its association with antioxidant peptide release and Keap1/Nrf2-related cellular responses. High-intensity ultrasound pretreatment (optimized at 450 W, 30 min, 30 mL/g) effectively deconstructed the dense interfacial architecture of VAP, sub-micronizing the particle size to  approximately 175 nm and promoting an ultrasound-associated conformational transition from alpha -helices to random coils. Thermodynamic deconstruction revealed that acoustic shear forces significantly attenuated the denaturation enthalpy (DeltaH) and elevated surface hydrophobicity (H(0)), alleviating steric constraints and driving an increase in targeted peptide yield from 44.82% to 68.32%. By integrating peptidomics, machine learning, and density functional theory (DFT), five representative antioxidant lead candidates were prioritized and subsequently synthesized for validation. DFT analyses suggested that these selected sequences may possess favorable electron-donating properties, potentially associated with aromatic residues, adjacent hydrophobic residues, and Pro-related conformational restriction. Furthermore, molecular docking suggested that these peptides may interact with the Keap1 Kelch domain, while in vitro cellular assays showed that the selected peptides restored endogenous antioxidant enzymes (SOD, CAT, GSH-Px) in H(2)O(2)-challenged RAW264.7 macrophages. These findings provide physicochemical and cellular evidence supporting ultrasound-assisted VAP modification and antioxidant peptide discovery, offering a laboratory-scale, mechanistically guided strategy for discovering functional peptides from structurally dense biological resources. Nevertheless, further pilot-scale validation is required before industrial translation.
abstract_zh: 从结构坚固的生物基质（如鹿茸蛋白 (velvet antler protein, VAP)）中靶向提取生物活性肽，受到高空间位阻和显著构象稳定性的严重阻碍。本研究建立了一个多尺度分析框架，以探究超声辅助VAP修饰及其与抗氧化肽释放和Keap1/Nrf2相关细胞响应的关联。高强度超声预处理（优化条件为450 W、30 min、30 mL/g）有效解构了VAP的致密界面结构，将粒径亚微米化至约175 nm，并促进了超声相关的构象转变，即从α-螺旋向无规卷曲的转化。热力学解构表明，声学剪切力显著降低了变性焓 (DeltaH) 并提高了表面疏水性 (H(0))，从而缓解了空间位阻，并将靶向肽得率从44.82%提升至68.32%。通过整合肽组学、机器学习和密度泛函理论 (density functional theory, DFT)，筛选出五个代表性抗氧化先导候选物，并随后合成以进行验证。DFT分析表明，这些选定序列可能具有有利的供电子特性，这可能与芳香族残基、邻近疏水残基及脯氨酸相关的构象限制有关。此外，分子对接提示这些肽可能与Keap1 Kelch结构域相互作用，而体外细胞实验显示，选定肽在H(2)O(2)刺激的RAW264.7巨噬细胞中恢复了内源性抗氧化酶（SOD、CAT、GSH-Px）的活性。这些发现为超声辅助VAP修饰和抗氧化肽发现提供了物理化学及细胞层面的证据，为从结构致密的生物资源中发现功能性肽提供了一种实验室规模、机制引导的策略。然而，在工业转化之前，仍需进一步的中试规模验证。
